rows.question: When does the trading blackout start before the end of a quarter?
rows.answer:
Trading blackouts apply automatically to all Grade L5+ personnel and designated finance/engineering staff commencing fifteen (15) calendar days prior to the close of each fiscal quarter and terminating forty-eight (48) hours after public dissemination of financial results.

Source: Section 1: Corporate Governance, Fiduciary Ethics & Conflict of Interest Architecture > 1.4 Insider Trading, Material Non-Public Information (MNPI) & Tipping Prohibitions (enterprise_company_policy_manual.docx)

rows.question: How long can an employee be suspended while an investigation is under way?
rows.answer:
Administrative Suspension & Equity Clawback Provisions: Where an employee is accused of a Category-A or serious Category-B offense, Human Resources and Legal may place the individual on paid (or unpaid where permitted by local statute) administrative suspension for up to fourteen (14) business days while forensic investigators secure evidence. If the investigation substantiates intentional financial misstatement, fraud, or gross supervisory negligence resulting in material reputational or regulatory harm, the Board Compensation Committee shall exercise its mandatory Clawback Policy to forfeit unvested equity awards and recover cash bonuses or vested shares paid during the preceding thirty-six (36) months. Appellate Review Procedure: Any employee subjected to a Formal Written Warning, demotion, suspension, or termination has the right to file a written Notice of Appeal within seven (7) business days of receiving the disciplinary decision.

Source: Section 14: Disciplinary Framework, Sanction Matrix, Appeals & Governance Audit > 14.3 Unstructured Narrative: Administrative Suspension, Executive Clawbacks & Right of Appeal (enterprise_company_policy_manual.docx)

rows.answer:

rows.question: Which cloud provider does the company use?
rows.answer:
All hardware endpoints, virtual machines, cloud tenant environments, source code repositories, corporate email accounts, instant messaging channels, and network bandwidth provisioned by the Enterprise remain the exclusive property of the company. Limited, incidental personal use of corporate devices (such as brief personal correspondence or medical appointment scheduling) is permitted strictly on a revocable privilege basis, provided it consumes negligible bandwidth, introduces zero malware or licensing risk, and never interferes with operational productivity. Users waive any expectation of personal privacy on corporate networks to the fullest extent permitted by local labor and data protection law.

Source: Section 3: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, ACCEPTABLE USE, CRYPTOGRAPHY & CYBERSECURITY ARCHITECTURE > 3.1 Enterprise Information Assets and Acceptable Use Doctrine (enterprise_company_policy_manual.txt)
